messages.author: d5fd91a345798d85
messages.subject: desiredtz
parts:
Hi Vincent, 

I had a question about the desiredtz arguement in the g.metadata function. Is the timezone used anywhere in the data processing or is just used to set a timestamp for the output file? I'm working with Actigraph GT3X+ data from across the US so there's about 3 timeszones I'm covering. I just set the desiredtz to "America/Los_Angeles" and processed all the data but I'm not sure if that's creating a problem in the processing or if it's altering the original timestamp in any way. I'm remerging these files to count files and to some machine-learned activity predictions and I'm seeing some timestamp mismatches at the beginnings of the files. Can I just shift the timestamp back? (e.g. if I process an East coast file with West coast desiredtz argument, will the timestamp be augmented?) 

Thanks!
Suni

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] desiredtz
parts:
Hi Suni,

Timestamps are used to identify midnights and by that to identify the
time window of a day, to label the summary data with correct dates and
to capture the starting time of the measurement. The timestamps are
not used for any other aspect of the analyses.

Timestamps formats are unfortunately different between accelerometer
brands/versions (Genea, Geneactiv, Actigraph) by which I had to come
up with a generic piece of code to account for all possible situations
(timezones and day saving time). I first made sure that the timestamps
are correctly interpreted for the study data I have been working on
myself and then only did a few tests with data from other timezones to
verify this.

It would be good if someone could critically review the timestamp
interpretation across accelerometer brands and identify where things
might go wrong.
I will try to look at this myself, but this could take a while.

Please note that if you compare your data with a second piece of
software then time may be interpreted differently by that other
software. My code relies on the sample frequency in combination with
the first timestamp while other software may rely on timestamps.
Sample frequency and timestamps are generated by a separate digital
clock. At the time I developed the code the Geneactiv accelerometer
had an unreliable clock for generating timestamps and an (on average)
reliable clock for generating sample frequency, which was why I relied
on sample frequency for describing time.

Thanks for raising the issue,

Vincent

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] desiredtz
parts:
Hi Sunni,

When data is summarised per epoch the epochs are not relative to the
start of the measurement but relative to specific seconds in a minute
or minutes in an hour. For example, a 15 minute epoch will always
start at 00, 15, 30, or 45 minutes past the hour. I do this to allow
for standardised comparison between days and person. So, if a
measurement starts at 6 minutes past the hour then the first 9 minutes
of the measurement are ignored such that the first recorded epoch
starts at 15 minutes past the hour and ends at 30 minutes past the
hour.

In your situation the code is undesirably doing something similar. It
does not recognise that you have a complete first 15 minutes, but
probably thinks that you have 14 minutes and 59 seconds, which makes
that those first block of data is not considered. This is obviously a
bug.

Thanks,

Vincent
